author: Editor (oa-editor), stage B round 2
purpose: The words chapter 10 prints beside each drawing in use, under DR-185, and one meaning sentence for each. The editor’s table of labels governs the words (round 2 brief).
label_rules: A topic symbol prints its Civic Line word in sentence case, the way Atlas V7 writes its names: Public meeting, Feedback loop, Contact an official. The words are the inventory’s; only the capitals change.
A pillar icon prints its pillar’s name: Explain, Track, Connect, Act. Chapter 09 governs them.

An atlas variable prints V7’s short name, the name V7 gives the variable on its loops, where V7 holds one (25 of 51); otherwise V7’s title (26 of 51). CL-025 reads Congress as a topic and Congressional capacity where it stands for D1 (DR-185).
An atlas reform prints V7’s title, except R-13, Congress’s own experts, and R-36, Lasting public investment, which DR-185 sets. R-35’s title keeps the word Rejected wherever it appears.
Labels and sentences use typographic apostrophes; v7_title keeps V7’s own characters for matching.
A typed chip names a V7 ID on a reader page, as Variable B3 or Reform R-01, never a bare code (H11).
meaning_rules: One full sentence per drawing: what it shows, then what it stands for, as the drawing is drawn now (the six redraws and the two new drawings as approved, DR-156 to DR-160).
Parts are named by shape and never by color, so each sentence holds for the one-color edition under 48 px, for a row where only the current drawing keeps its red, and for the Black files.
An atlas symbol’s sentence says what V7’s element is in V7’s own terms, and defines V7’s short name where it is a term of art, such as affective polarization (H02).
Numbers under ten are words (H06); no em dashes (W21).

rows.v7_name: Public and philanthropic funding for local news
rows.label: Public and philanthropic funding for local news
rows.meaning: A stack of coins beside a newspaper stands for public and foundation money that pays for reporting on local government.

rows.v7_title: Citizen assemblies that officials must answer
rows.v7_name: Citizen assemblies that officials must answer
rows.label: Citizen assemblies that officials must answer
rows.meaning: Five people around an oval table make up a citizen assembly, residents chosen by lottery who study a public question and get a public answer from officials.

rows.v7_title: Participatory budgeting: residents decide spending
rows.v7_name: Participatory budgeting: residents decide spending
rows.label: Participatory budgeting: residents decide spending
rows.meaning: People stand in front of a checklist with boxes ticked, for residents who propose projects and vote on how to spend part of a city’s budget.

rows.v7_title: Rejected option: term limits for legislators
rows.v7_name: Rejected option: term limits for legislators
rows.label: Rejected option: term limits for legislators
rows.meaning: A disc with a cross over the clock behind an officeholder marks term limits for legislators, an option the atlas rejects because studies of state legislatures find that limits weaken how a legislature works.

rows.v7_title: Lasting public investment in research and infrastructure
rows.v7_name: Lasting public investment in research and infrastructure
rows.label: Lasting public investment
rows.label_source: DR-185, a short form of V7’s title
rows.meaning: A lightbulb, a bridge and a funding record stand in a row, for funding research and infrastructure over several years and protecting that money until projects are finished.

rows.v7_title: Feed choice and data access for researchers
rows.v7_name: Feed choice and data access for researchers
rows.label: Feed choice and data access for researchers
rows.meaning: A browser window with a slider stands beside a key, for letting users choose how their feeds are ranked and letting researchers study platform data.

rows.v7_title: Limits on pricing software using rivals' data
rows.v7_name: Limits on pricing software using rivals’ data
rows.label: Limits on pricing software using rivals’ data
rows.meaning: A prohibition sign cutting the dashed link between two price tags stands for barring pricing software from using competitors’ private data to set prices.

rows.v7_title: Government teams that build digital services
rows.v7_name: Government teams that build digital services
rows.label: Government teams that build digital services
rows.meaning: Two people stand beside a screen holding an ID and a form, for the government’s own technology teams, who build the software people use to claim benefits, get tax refunds and apply for permits.

rows.v7_title: Notice and a voice for workers on AI
rows.v7_name: Notice and a voice for workers on AI
rows.label: Notice and a voice for workers on AI
rows.meaning: A worker speaks up beside a chip marked AI, for telling workers when AI helps hire, schedule or rate them, and giving them a say in how it is used.

rows.v7_title: Large power users pay their grid costs
rows.v7_name: Large power users pay their grid costs
rows.label: Large power users pay their grid costs
rows.meaning: A row of servers plugs into a bill marked with a dollar sign, for making large new power users such as data centers pay for the grid upgrades their demand requires.

rows.v7_title: Congress votes on lasting tariffs
rows.v7_name: Congress votes on lasting tariffs
rows.label: Congress votes on lasting tariffs
rows.meaning: A chamber in session sits above a vote card marked yes and no and a tagged parcel, for tariffs, taxes on imports, that last beyond a short period only if Congress approves them.
rows.drawn_as: Redrawn, approved by name: DR-156, set B

rows.v7_title: Building codes and mitigation against disaster losses
rows.v7_name: Building codes and mitigation against disaster losses
rows.label: Building codes and mitigation against disaster losses
rows.meaning: A house with a strengthened roof, under a storm and above floodwater, shows stronger building codes and upgrades that cut the damage when disaster strikes.

rows.v7_title: Competition remedies for search and ad markets
rows.v7_name: Competition remedies for search and ad markets
rows.label: Competition remedies for search and ad markets
rows.meaning: Two browser windows, each with a search magnifier, pass arrows both ways, for remedies that open search and online advertising to rival companies.

rows.v7_title: Verifiable elections with paper records and audits
rows.v7_name: Verifiable elections with paper records and audits
rows.label: Verifiable elections with paper records and audits
rows.meaning: Paper ballots under a magnifier with a check stand for elections in which every vote leaves a paper record and results are audited.

rows.v7_title: Expand the House of Representatives
rows.v7_name: Expand the House of Representatives
rows.label: Expand the House of Representatives
rows.meaning: Seats added along the outer row of a chamber seen from above show a larger House, where each member represents fewer people.

rows.v7_title: Fusion voting and public funding for parties
rows.v7_name: Fusion voting and public funding for parties
rows.label: Fusion voting and public funding for parties
rows.meaning: Lines from two candidate cards meet at one person between them, for letting more than one party nominate the same candidate, with public funding for parties.

rows.v7_title: Agency independence after the Slaughter ruling
rows.v7_name: Agency independence after the Slaughter ruling
rows.label: Agency independence after the Slaughter ruling
rows.meaning: An arrow from an official at a desk stops at a brace before a commission at its table, for Congress protecting independent agencies after the Supreme Court’s June 2026 ruling in Trump v. Slaughter.
rows.drawn_as: Redrawn, approved by name: DR-158, option C

rows.v7_title: Civic work that crosses party lines
rows.v7_name: Civic work that crosses party lines
rows.label: Civic work that crosses party lines
rows.meaning: An arc and a small bridge join two people, for groups that bring people of different parties together for shared work, such as serving as poll workers.

rows.v7_title: Popular-vote compact and constitutional amendment options
rows.v7_name: Popular-vote compact and constitutional amendment options
rows.label: Popular-vote compact and constitutional amendment options
rows.meaning: A brace gathers four ballots above a map of the United States, for the National Popular Vote compact and constitutional amendments that would change how presidents and senators are chosen.
